messages:
alice: heads-up — we saw another short saturation spike on eu-west last night around 02:13 UTC. queue depth hit ~1.4k and admission rejections spiked to 11.7%. :grimacing:
ben: ouch. any idea what triggered it? sudden burst from a partner?
carmen: logs show a synchronous batch job in eu-west1 from partner X that ramped from 200 qps -> 1.6k qps in ~40s. warm pool tried to scale but median GPU spinup is 52s there.
raj: that spinup number matches our infra metrics — preemptible VMs are taking longer because of regional API throttling. also kernel modules sometimes take extra time on that family.
sophie: did admission control stop the queue growing?
alice: partially — admission token bucket kicked in but burst size allowed a large transient. token refill rate was 120 tokens/sec across the region, burst=500 tokens, which let the initial surge through before warm nodes were ready.
ben: so we have two levers: increase warm_pool (cost) or tighten admission/burst (higher immediate rejects). prefer smoothness vs cost?
carmen: propose a hybrid: slightly increase min warm GPUs in eu-west (from 6 -> 10) and reduce token burst to 250, refill to 80/s. That should absorb short blips without holding too many idle GPUs.
raj: can we instead do adaptive warmup based on per-customer QPS history? e.g., detect rising gradient and pre-provision extra nodes proactively.
sophie: that's long-term. quick fix needs config changes plus a canary rollout. also we should throttle the partner job if possible. @partner-eng reached out?
alice: partner-eng pinged them this morning; they said the job was an analytics backfill they kicked off accidentally. partner agreed to add a throttling flag.
ben: what about admission smoothing — change token bucket to per-backend pool rather than global region? that avoids noisy neighbor effects.
carmen: good call. per-backend token buckets + per-pool warm sizing. config snippet I tested locally: 
```
warm_pool_configs:
  eu-west:
    min_idle_gpus: 10
    max_idle_gpus: 20
    scale_timeout_secs: 180
admission_control:
  eu-west:
    token_rate: 80/s
    burst: 250
    per_backend: true
```
raj: looks fine. what about the effect on cost — rough numbers?
ben: bumping min_idle from 6->10 in eu-west (N=4 extra A100s) is ~ $3.2/hr extra. Monthly ~ $2.3k. If this avoids 1 outage a month, probably worth it.
sophie: add dashboards and alerts for the canary: queue_depth > 800 for >60s OR admitted_rejections >5% should rollback.
alice: plan: 1) apply per-backend token bucket + reduced burst in eu-west as a small canary (10% of traffic) 2) increase warm_pool min_idle in canary region subset 3) monitor 1h, rollback if alerts fire.
ben: timeline?
carmen: I'll prepare a config PR now. canary rollout via deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued for eng-infra, change set: admission/eu-west per-backend + warm_pool delta. runbook: monitor infra.queue_depth, infra.admit_reject_rate, node.spinup_latency.
raj: add a synthetic load that simulates partner pattern into canary to validate behavior. I'll run it 15m after deploy.
sophie: make sure cost dashboard has the warm-pool increase flagged so finance sees it.
alice: agreed. if canary looks good after 1h, we roll region-wide. rollback criteria: sustained reject >5% or 95th latency > target by >150ms.
ben: also add a slow ramp for token_rate changes to avoid oscillation: change by max 20% every 2 minutes.
carmen: noted. PR will include that pacing.
infra-bot: alert rule created: canary-eu-west-warmup -> notify #eng-oncall if queue_depth>800 for 60s.
alice: thanks. assigning follow-ups: carmen PR, raj synthetic test, sophie cost tag, ben monitor tweaks. check back in 90m. :thumbsup:
